title: Wei
capsule: Wei (魏) was one of the Three Jins, formed when Zhou's King Weilie formally recognized the partition of the old state of Jin among the Wei, Han, and Zhao ministerial clans in 403 BCE. Under Marquess Wen and King Hui, Wei was briefly the strongest Warring State, ruling first from Anyi and later from Daliang (modern Kaifeng), and its scholars helped seed the Legalist statecraft that Qin later adopted. Weakened by wars on multiple fronts, Wei fell in 225 BCE when the Qin general Wang Ben diverted the Yellow River to flood its capital.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Cao Wei's territory in northern China is well documented by the administrative geography of its commandery system, itself inherited from the Han census; the fluctuating southern frontiers contested with Shu Han and Eastern Wu are attested by campaign records but are imprecisely rendered as fixed lines.
